text: Study Sources 1 and 2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘There are many benefits of learning outside of the classroom.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘Most teachers do not take their students outside the classroom.’
How could you test this claim? You may consider the types of information, sources of evidence
or methods you might use.

text: Study Source 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify one prediction from Tuaco’s statement.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Identify one value judgement from Abina’s statement. Explain why it is a value judgement.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Tuaco’s or Abina’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different types of information used.

text: Study Source 4.
A local school would like to improve the quality of education for all learners.
The following suggestions have been made:
• improve the literacy skills of younger learners
• increase opportunities to learn outside the classroom
• improve preparation for examinations so that learners gain more qualifications.
Which one of these suggestions do you think is likely to have the most impact, and why?
In your answer you should:
• state your preferred suggestion
• give reasons to support your choice
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
• consider different arguments and perspectives.
